title: Listen (Rule, Prologue)
hookLine: the Rule begins with listen, with the ear of your heart

lines: A NEW BLOCK: THE GREAT ORDERS.
cards: Nod. Say mm-hm. Plan your reply while the other person is still talking.

Half-listening takes almost no effort, and it can pass for the real thing for a long time. A new block begins today: the great religious orders, the communities of monks, friars and sisters who share a way of life.
First, the Benedictines, and a small book written for monks in Italy long ago. Its very first word is not pray. Not work.

teach.b: Back on day eighty-seven you met Benedict and his sister Scholastica, his twin, tradition says. Tradition gives him the Rule, a short book to guide monks living together in Italy. Monks call it simply the Rule.
It covers prayer and work, meals and sleep, guests and the sick, and how to settle a quarrel. But it opens like a letter from a father to a son. In Latin: inclina aurem cordis tui.

teach.h: BEND DOWN THE EAR OF YOUR HEART.
teach.b: Listen, my son, to the teaching of the master, and bend down the ear of your heart. It's the posture of someone leaning in to catch a quiet voice, a parent bent over a cot.
And it's the ear of the heart, not just the ears on your head: letting what you hear reach the place where you decide things.

The Prologue says this listening should turn into doing, and that the one speaking is finally God. It borrows a psalm, in the Douay-Rheims: "To day if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts." Notice the order.
Before the long list of chapters, before the schedule, before a single bell rings, there's a posture: lean in.

teach.h: A RULE IS A WAY OF LISTENING.
teach.b: A rule, for Benedict, isn't a cage of instructions.
It's a shared way of listening, kept day after day, so a whole community can hear together.
Benedictine monks and nuns still read the Rule aloud together, and each time they come back around to its start, the first thing they hear is: listen.

how: Benedictine monks and nuns hear passages of the Rule read aloud in community, and oblates and other laypeople read it at home.

games.q: you're Benedict, writing the first word of a rule for monks. which do you choose?
games.why: the Rule opens: listen, my son, and bend down the ear of your heart. before the bells and the schedule, a posture.

practice: Start with the sounds around you, the hum of a room, a car outside, your own breathing, and just lean toward them, without naming or judging.

Then bring to mind the person you'll talk with next, and imagine giving them that same attention: no planning your reply, no phone, just leaning in. If you pray, ask to hear God's voice in whatever comes.
